question: Which of the following yagna is related to the sacrifice of the horse?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashwamedh Yagna**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashwamedh Yagna** is a ritual of horse sacrifice that was historically conducted by ancient Indian kings.
 
• The yagna is mentioned in various ancient Indian texts, including the Vedas and the Mahabharata.
 
• The purpose of the Ashwamedh Yagna was to establish the supremacy of the king performing the ritual over other kings and regions.
 
• In this ritual, a horse was set free to wander for a year, accompanied by the king's warriors. The territories the horse wandered into had to either accept the king's supremacy or challenge it in battle.
 
• The successful completion of the yagna symbolized the king's undisputed sovereignty and divine favor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vajpayee Yagna** is another type of Vedic ritual, but it is not related to horse sacrifice.
 
• **Agnishom Yagna** is a Vedic ritual involving offerings to fire, but it does not involve a horse.
 
• **Rajsuya Yagna** is a royal consecration ceremony performed by a king, but it does not involve the sacrifice of a horse.
